name: Question 5
problem: Find the equation of the tangent plane to the surface $z=\sqrt{xy}+xy$ at the point $(2,2,6).$
worked_solution:
The Cartesian equation of the tangent plane to the surface $z=f(x,y)$ at the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$ on the surface can be written as

$$
z-{z}_{0}=(x-{x}_{0})\frac{∂f}{∂x}({x}_{0},{y}_{0})+(y-{y}_{0})\frac{∂f}{∂y}({x}_{0},{y}_{0}).
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\sqrt{xy}+xy) \\  & =\frac{y}{2\sqrt{xy}}+y \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{y}}{2\sqrt{x}}+y \\ \frac{∂f}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(\sqrt{xy}+xy) \\  & =\frac{x}{2\sqrt{xy}}+x \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{x}}{2\sqrt{y}}+x\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate the partial derivatives at $(x,y)=(2,2):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x}(2,2) & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2\sqrt{2}}+2=\frac{5}{2} \\ \frac{∂f}{∂y}(2,2) & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2\sqrt{2}}+2=\frac{5}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we write down the equation of the tangent plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}z-6 & =(x-2)\frac{∂f}{∂x}(2,2)+(y-2)\frac{∂f}{∂y}(2,2) \\ z-6 & =\frac{5}{2}(x-2)+\frac{5}{2}(y-2) \\ z-6 & =\frac{5x}{2}+\frac{5y}{2}-10 \\ 2z-12 & =5x+5y-20 \\ -5x-5y+2z+8 & =0 \\ 5x+5y-2z-8 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Question 5
?

Find the equation of the tangent plane to the surface z=xy+xy at the point (2,2,6).

a
5x+5y−2z+14=0
b
5x+5y−z−4=0
c
5x+5y−2z−8=0
d
5x−5y+2z−36=0
e
5x−5y−2z−8=0
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The Cartesian equation of the tangent plane to the surface z=f(x,y) at the point (x0,y0,z0) on the surface can be written as

z−z0=(x−x0)∂f∂x(x0,y0)+(y−y0)∂f∂y(x0,y0).

First, we find the partial derivatives:

∂f∂x=∂∂x(xy+xy)=y2xy+y=y2x+y∂f∂y=∂∂y(xy+xy)=x2xy+x=x2y+x

Next, we evaluate the partial derivatives at (x,y)=(2,2):

∂f∂x(2,2)=222+2=52∂f∂y(2,2)=222+2=52

Finally, we write down the equation of the tangent plane:

z−6=(x−2)∂f∂x(2,2)+(y−2)∂f∂y(2,2)z−6=52(x−2)+52(y−2)z−6=5x2+5y2−102z−12=5x+5y−20−5x−5y+2z+8=05x+5y−2z−8=0
